subject: Clarifying 'Derivative' & non-modeling-use carveout in DPA
messages:
From: Avery Chen <avery.chen@clearpointtx.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: samir.desai@clearpointtx.com, legal@clearpointtx.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: definition of 'Derivatives' and training carveout

Karthik —

Thanks for sending the redline last week. Our legal team flagged the new definition in Section 2 ("Derivatives") and the added training carveout language in Section 6.2. We appreciate Redwood's effort to limit model training, but the current draft still reads as permitting use of "Derivative Data" for model improvement unless explicitly excluded.

Can you confirm whether "Derivative Data" (as currently defined) would include sanitized, aggregated telemetry and anonymized customer prompts that ClearPoint sends for debugging? We need clarity because our security team will not approve any clause that could be interpreted to allow model training on telemetry tied to our tenant even after anonymization.

Attached: our annotated redline (ClearPoint_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) with highlights on page 4-6.

Proposed ask from our side: either (a) expressly prohibit using any data derived from customer-provided inputs for model training/model-improvement, or (b) allow only a narrow, auditable telemetry-use path limited to operational debugging with explicit retention and deletion windows. Which option aligns with Redwood's policy?

Thanks,
Avery Chen
Director, Information Security
ClearPoint Therapeutics

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@clearpointtx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: definition of 'Derivatives' and training carveout

Avery —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the annotated PDF. Short answer: Redwood's standard position is that we do not train foundation models on customer data unless specifically permitted in a signed DPA/execution path. That said, operational telemetry and anonymized/aggregated metrics are handled differently because they're often necessary to keep the service healthy.

A couple of clarifications:
- "Derivative Data" in our redline was intended to mean data *compiled* from customer inputs where no tenant-identifying metadata remains. It was NOT intended to include raw prompts or tenant-tagged logs.
- We can offer a firm carveout: no customer-provided inputs, nor derivatives that can be reverse-correlated to a tenant, will be used for model training or continual model improvement.

Options for ClearPoint:
1) Explicit ban (preferred for regulated customers): add a clause that prohibits using customer inputs or any derivative data that can be correlated back to the customer for model training.
2) Operational telemetry allowance: allow ephemeral use of strictly operational telemetry for debugging and SRE purposes only, scoped by access controls and automatic deletion after X days (we suggest 30 by default).

I'll loop in Marissa (Legal) and Neha (Product) to draft precise language. If you prefer, we can redline option 1 and 2 as alternatives in the DPA.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@clearpointtx.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: definition of 'Derivatives' and training carveout

Avery —

Thanks for raising the telemetry question. Per Karthik's note, Redwood is comfortable with a conservative approach for ClearPoint. Draft proposal (high level):

- Section 2 (Definitions): Add a definition for "Derivative Data" that explicitly excludes any data that (a) contains tenant identifiers, (b) can be reasonably re-associated with ClearPoint users or accounts, or (c) was produced by models trained on ClearPoint inputs.

- Section 6.2 (Model Use / Training): Add the sentence: "Provider shall not use Customer Data or any Derivative Data that can be correlated to Customer for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, or improving Provider's models, unless Customer provides prior written consent via the Agreement or an executed amendment."

- Operational telemetry carveout: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may use ephemeral, aggregated operational telemetry strictly for system health and debugging, provided that such telemetry (i) is stored in an access-restricted environment, (ii) is retained no longer than thirty (30) days by default, and (iii) is auditable by Customer upon request in accordance with the audit process set forth in Exhibit B."

We will prepare two redline tracks: (A) strict prohibition track for customers that want a no-training guarantee, and (B) restricted telemetry track that includes the retention window and audit hooks. Which track does ClearPoint prefer us to send to your counsel?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Chen <avery.chen@clearpointtx.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: samir.desai@clearpointtx.com, legal@clearpointtx.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: definition of 'Derivatives' and training carveout

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks, that's helpful. ClearPoint's compliance team prefers option A (strict prohibition). Two follow-ups: (1) we need explicit language preventing downstream subprocessor use of any such data for training, and (2) we'd like to confirm whether Redwood keeps a public (or customer-accessible) list of subprocessors and how subprocessor changes are communicated.

On (1): if you can insert a line that prohibits Provider and Provider's subprocessors from using Customer Data or Correlatable Derivative Data for model training without Customer's written consent, that'll address our primary concern.

On (2): please attach your current subprocessor roster and indicate the change-notice period.

Avery

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@clearpointtx.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: definition of 'Derivatives' and training carveout

Avery —

We reviewed and updated the redline per your preference for option A. Highlights of the changes (attached in ClearPoint_DPA_redline_v3.pdf):

- Added explicit clause: "Provider and its subprocessors shall not use Customer Data, nor any Derivative Data that can be correlated to Customer, for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, or otherwise improving any machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent."

- Added subprocessor clause: "Provider will not permit subprocessors to use Customer Data or Correlatable Derivative Data for model training; any required use must be subject to the same contractual restrictions as between Provider and Customer."

- Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (subprocessors_list_2026-07.csv). We provide ≥30 days notice prior to onboarding a new subprocessor that may access Customer Data; critical security updates or emergency switches are handled according to Section 9.4 (emergency transition) with immediate notice to Customer.

Next steps: if this version is acceptable, we can prepare execution copies. We'll include a DocuSign envelope (stub attached) for signature routing to your GC.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you'd like to review the redline together.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Product & Privacy
Redwood Inference
